paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the best thing you could ever have is knowing Christ, and nothing on your résumé comes close. Paul had the list, and he says himself that he had more grounds for confidence than anyone (Philippians 3:4). Then he says, "But whatever was gain to me I count as loss for the sake of Christ" (Philippians 3:7). He calls it "rubbish" next to "the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord" (Philippians 3:8).

So why does that matter to you? Because we all keep a list. Our work, our record, our good deeds, all stacked up like a tray of cookies we hope looks impressive. Paul says he doesn't want "my own righteousness from the law," but "the righteousness from God on the basis of faith" (Philippians 3:9). I spent years thinking my worth was my sharp edges, and Papa Dorin was WRONG about that, friend.

And look at what Paul wants instead. He wants "to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings" (Philippians 3:10). Knowing Him is the prize, and it's not a one-time thing. Paul keeps reaching for it, so you can keep reaching too, and you can set the list down and rejoice in the Lord (Philippians 3:1).
